pinterest.title: Wedding Timeline for a 4pm Ceremony: An Example Day, Hour by Hour
pinterest.description: A wedding timeline for a 4pm ceremony in two example versions. With a first look, hair and makeup might begin at 9am and the couple and wedding party photos are done before guests arrive at 3.30pm. Without one, it might begin at 10am and the photos follow the ceremony, so the reception starts later in the evening. Every clock time is a planning example to adapt to your team, your venue and your sunset.

pinterest.title: 4pm Wedding Ceremony Timeline: Plan Your Photos Around Sunset
pinterest.description: Sunset is the anchor for a 4pm wedding timeline. Look it up for your venue on your date, not the nearest city, using Geoscience Australia's sunrise, sunset and twilight calculator, then work back: portraits finish around sunset, drinks sit either side and the reception entrance follows. With hills, trees or buildings to the west, the sun drops out of view before the listed time, so walk the site at the same hour.

pinterest.title: Wedding Timeline Template for a 4pm Ceremony, Ready to Copy
pinterest.description: A wedding timeline template you can copy into a document or spreadsheet. Start with three lines for your venue and date: sunset, the end of civil twilight (lighting on before this) and the end of nautical twilight (guests moved or routes lit before this). Then fill in hair and makeup, first look, guest arrival, ceremony, family photos, drinks, reception, speeches, first dance and the venue curfew, with who needs to be there and where.

slides: Planning a 4pm ceremony? Start with one time: sunset at your venue on your wedding date. Everything else is worked back from it.
Look it up for the venue itself, not the nearest city. Geoscience Australia's sunrise, sunset and twilight calculator gives sunset and twilight times for a place and a date.
An example day with a first look: hair and makeup from 9am, first look at 2pm, guests arrive at 3.30pm, ceremony at 4pm, reception entrance at 6pm. Times to adapt, not rules.
An example day without one: hair and makeup from 10am, family photos straight after the ceremony, couple portraits at 5.30pm, reception entrance and entrée at 6.30pm.
Put the buffer at the handovers: 15 minutes before the dress goes on, ten minutes for hugs after the ceremony, a quarter hour before the reception entrance.
Have the festoons, candles and uplights on before evening civil twilight ends, not after guests notice the dark.
Thinking 2pm, 3pm or 5pm instead? The light, the heat, the gap before dinner and how guests travel all move with it. At 5pm, check the venue's curfew first.

instagram_carousel.caption:
The one time that sets a 4pm wedding day is sunset at your venue on your date. Look it up first, then build the photos, the lighting and the reception entrance around it.

Our new guide sets out a 4pm ceremony hour by hour in two example versions:

With a first look, the couple and wedding party photos happen before 4pm, so you join your guests for drinks.

Without one, the photos follow the ceremony and the reception starts later in the evening. Ask the venue to hold canapés and a drink for you both.

Every clock time in it is a planning example to adapt. Your team, your venue and your sunset will each move them.

For sunset, use Geoscience Australia's sunrise, sunset and twilight calculator, and look up the single day of your wedding at the venue itself. If there are hills, trees or buildings to the west, the sun drops out of view before the listed time.

The guide also covers what changes at 2pm, 3pm and 5pm, where the buffer belongs, questions to ask a destination venue about curfews and same-day guest arrivals, and a timeline template to copy.

Planning a destination wedding? A Wedded Advisor works in your time zone and is your single point of contact for the venue questions. Start the conversation with Wedded Concierge.

Read the full guide via the link in our bio.
